items.title: Section: A Second Framework — Ten Conditions That Favour Training

items.zh: 復有十種隨順學法。何等為十？一者、宿因，二者、隨順教，三者、如理加行，四者、無間殷重所作，五者、猛利樂欲，六者、持瑜伽力，七者、止息身心麁重，八者、數數觀察，九者、無有怯弱，十者、離增上慢。云何宿因？謂先所習諸根成熟、諸根積集。云何隨順教？謂所說教無倒、漸次。云何如理加行？謂如其教無倒修行，如是修行能生正見。云何無間、殷重所作？謂由如是正加行故，於諸善品不虛捨命，速能積習所有善品。云何猛利樂欲？謂如有一，於上解脫發生希慕。謂我何時當於是處能具足住，如諸聖者於是處所具足而住。云何持瑜伽力？謂二因緣能令獲得持瑜伽力。一者、本性是利根故；二者、長時串修習故。云何止息身心麁重？謂如有一，或由身勞身乏，發身麁重，發心麁重；此因易脫威儀而便止息。或由太尋太伺，發身麁重、發心麁重；此因內心寂止方便而便止息。或由心略心劣，惛沈睡眠之所纏遶、發身麁重、發心麁重；此因增上慧法毘鉢舍那順淨作意而便止息。或由本性煩惱未斷，有煩惱品身心麁重未能捨離；此因相續勤修正道而便止息。
items.en: There are, further, ten kinds of conduct favouring training: past causes; conduct according with instruction; correct application; work done without interruption and with earnest care; intense aspiration; sustaining the power of yogic practice; calming grossness of body and mind; repeated examination; freedom from timidity; and freedom from overestimation. … As for one whose bodily grossness and mental grossness arise from bodily fatigue and exhaustion — this is calmed simply by changing posture. As for one in whom it arises from excessive initial and sustained thought — this is calmed through the technique of inner calm-abiding. As for one in whom it arises from a contracted, feeble mind entangled in dullness and drowsiness — this is calmed through the higher-wisdom technique of insight practice, engaging the mind towards what is purifying. As for one in whom it arises because the underlying afflictions themselves remain uncut — this is calmed through sustained, diligent cultivation of the correct path.

items.title: Section: Conduct in Accordance with Training Closes

items.zh: 謂依尸羅，數數觀察惡作不作，數數觀察善作而作。於其惡作不作不轉；於其善作不作不退。於其惡作作而棄捨，於其善作作而不捨。又於煩惱斷與未斷觀察作意增上力故，數數觀察。若知已斷，便生歡喜；若知未斷，則便數數勤修正道。云何無有怯弱？謂於後時應知、應見、應證得中，未知、未見、未證得故，發生怯弱，其心勞倦、其心匱損，彼既生已而不堅執，速能斷滅。云何離增上慢？謂於所得、所觸、所證，無增上慢，離顛倒執。於真所得起於得想，於真所觸起於觸想，於真所證起於證想。
items.en: Repeated examination based on discipline means repeatedly checking that one has not committed what should not be done, and has continued what should be done. Repeated examination based on mental engagement means, by the power of examining whether affliction has or has not been cut off, checking again and again: if one finds it has been cut off, gladness arises; if one finds it has not, one diligently cultivates the correct path once more. What is freedom from timidity? It is this: even when discouragement arises upon finding that what should eventually be known, seen, and realised remains as yet unknown, unseen, and unrealized — leaving the mind weary and depleted — once this discouragement has arisen, not clinging to it, but swiftly letting it dissolve. What is freedom from overestimation? It is having no inflated conceit regarding what one has attained, touched, or realised, free of any distorted grasping — forming the notion of "attained" only where something is truly attained, "touched" only where truly touched, "realised" only where truly realised.

items.zh: 如是十法，於樂修學諸瑜伽師所應修學，初中後時恒常隨順，無有違逆，是故名為隨順學法。

items.title: Section: The Failure of Yogic Practice Opens — Four Kinds

items.zh: 云何瑜伽壞？謂壞瑜伽略有四種。何等為四？一者、畢竟瑜伽壞，二者、暫時瑜伽壞，三者、退失所得瑜伽壞，四者、邪行所作瑜伽壞。畢竟瑜伽壞者，謂無種姓補持伽羅。何以故？由彼身中無能趣向涅槃法故，畢竟失壞出世瑜伽。
items.en: What is the failure of yogic practice? Briefly, the failure of yogic practice is of four kinds. What are the four? Final failure; temporary failure; failure through the regression of what has been attained; and failure brought about by wrong conduct. Final failure refers to a person without the lineage for liberation. Why? Because within such a person there is no capacity that tends towards nirvana, and so the supramundane yogic practice is finally and completely lost to them.

items.zh: 暫時瑜伽壞者，謂有種姓補特伽羅。何以故？

items.title: Temporary Failure and the Regression of Attainment

items.zh: 由彼身中有能趣向涅槃法故，雖闕外緣，時經久遠，定當緣會；修習瑜伽，令其現起；善修習已，當般涅槃。是故說彼所有瑜伽暫時失壞。退失所得瑜伽壞者，謂如有一，退失所得、所觸、所證，若智、若見、若安樂住。
items.en: Because within such a person there is a capacity tending towards nirvana, even lacking the outer conditions for now, given enough time these conditions will certainly come together; yogic practice will be cultivated and caused to arise, and once well cultivated, nirvana will be attained. This is why such a person's yogic practice is said to be only temporarily lost. Failure through the regression of what has been attained refers to one who loses what has been attained, touched, or realised — the knowledge, the vision, or the peaceful abiding that went with it.

blocks.text: What supports training, and four ways in which yogic practice can fail.

Past causes; conduct according with instruction; correct application; continuous and careful work; knowing when to calm, rouse, and let be; removing grossness of body and mind; and repeated examination. Master Cháng Bǎi: grossness has four sources: bodily fatigue, too much thought, too much joy, too much sleep. Venerable Miào Jìng: the growth of wholesome roots in past lives is a real support now.

Based on discipline: "repeatedly checking that one has not done what should not be done". Based on concentration: checking whether the absorptions have been attained. Based on wisdom: checking whether afflictions have been cut. "If one finds it has been cut off, gladness arises; if not, one diligently cultivates."

items: **Final failure**: one lacking the lineage for nirvāṇa; "the supramundane yogic practice is never attained". Venerable Miào Jìng: no seed of the noble path in the ālayavijñāna.
**Temporary failure**: one with the capacity, but without the outer conditions for now; "given enough time, these conditions will come together".
**Regression**: losing a worldly attainment through heedlessness. Venerable Miào Jìng: the noble path, once attained, cannot be lost.

quiz.q: In the second framework of ten favourable conditions, what comes first, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: past causes; past cultivation now ripening, the roots of faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom growing
quiz.why: "Past causes; conduct according with instruction; correct application …" Venerable Miào Jìng: the growth of wholesome roots is what "past causes" means. He encourages practitioners not to lose heart when progress is slow — past cultivation will ripen.

quiz.q: The text names uncut innate afflictions as the fourth source of grossness. How does Master Cháng Bǎi summarise the four sources?
options: fatigue, too much thought, torpor, agitation — he lists agitation fourth, where the text has uncut afflictions, calmed by diligent cultivation of the path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: grossness of body and mind has four sources — bodily fatigue; initial and sustained thought, thinking too much; torpor and drowsiness; agitation. The text's fourth is uncut innate afflictions, remedied by sustained cultivation of the path; he then adds that for heavy afflictions one trains in discipline, concentration, and wisdom.

quiz.q: Why must one examine "again and again" whether affliction is cut off, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: afflictions sometimes lie still — not cut but seeming so; one look is unreliable, so look again and again
quiz.why: "If one finds it has been cut off, gladness arises; if one finds it has not, one diligently cultivates the correct path once more." Venerable Miào Jìng: a person may not have cut off affliction, yet it is not stirring now — so it seems cut off, as if eliminated.

quiz.q: "No inflated conceit regarding what one has attained, touched, or realised." How do the masters map these three?
options: Miào Jìng maps to absorptions: first = attained, second = touched, third and fourth = realised; Cháng Bǎi adds the supramundane: first fruit, second and third, arhatship
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one may say the first absorption is "attained," the second "touched," the third and fourth "realised." Master Cháng Bǎi: in terms of the supramundane path, "attained" is the first fruit, "touched" the second and third, "realised" arhatship. Overestimation is mistaking the first absorption for the first fruit.

quiz.q: What are the four failures of yogic practice, and how broad does Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the commentary, say the failure is?
options: final, temporary, regression, wrong conduct; not only calm and insight but all of discipline, concentration, and wisdom are ruined
quiz.why: "Final failure; temporary failure; failure through the regression of what has been attained; and failure brought about by wrong conduct." Master Cháng Bǎi: in the commentary's explanation, failure is not only the ruin of calm and insight — discipline, concentration, and wisdom are all ruined.

quiz.q: Final failure is a person without the lineage. What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: no seed of the supramundane path in the storehouse consciousness; Cháng Bǎi: such people are still the Buddha's concern, but can be led only to human and divine realms
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: within such a person's storehouse consciousness there is no seed of the supramundane noble path — this is final failure. Master Cháng Bǎi: as a skilful teaching, this treatise holds that those without the lineage are still beings the Buddha guides, but only into the good destinies of humans and gods.

quiz.q: In failure through regression, what is lost, and can the noble path be lost? What do the masters say?
options: both: absorption is lost; in this treatise the path is not. Cháng Bǎi notes some schools held the second and third fruits could regress
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the noble path cannot be lost; from the Yogācārabhūmi's standpoint, once attained it does not regress. Master Cháng Bǎi: some schools say the first and fourth fruits don't regress but the second and third can; this treatise says the noble path does not regress, but absorption can.
